Toroidal coordinates ​

See also

Theory: Toroidal functions · Curvilinear differential calculus

Manual: Coordinate systems (symbolic) · Charts and coordinate conversions · Toroidal functions

A torus is the surface swept by a circle that revolves about an axis of its plane. The toroidal coordinates are the orthogonal system in which a family of tori sharing a focal circle is a family of coordinate surfaces: the natural system for a ring-shaped inclusion or a toroidal pore. This page builds the system with the steps of Curvilinear differential calculus, writes its differential operators, separates the Laplace equation and describes a torus seen as a surface.
